title: Bona Vacantia — Crown Ownerless Property

sections.heading: What is bona vacantia?
sections.content:
Bona vacantia (Latin: ownerless goods) refers to land and property that has passed to the Crown because:

- The previous owner died intestate (without a will) with no known heirs, or
- A company that owned the land was dissolved without transferring it.

sections.heading: Can you buy it?
sections.content:
Yes — but it is a genuine purchase at market value, not a free acquisition. You must approach the Bona Vacantia Division (BVD) of the Government Legal Department and express interest in purchasing the land. The BVD has discretion to decline or disclaim the land.

If the BVD disclaims interest, the land escheats to the Crown Estate and a new freehold title must be granted.

sections.heading: Data availability note
sections.content:
The BVD unclaimed estates list was temporarily removed from GOV.UK in July 2025 following a fraud investigation. Its availability and format are subject to change. Always verify current status directly with the BVD before proceeding.

BVD website: https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/bona-vacantia

sections.heading: Dissolved company land
sections.content:
Land owned by a dissolved company may also be subject to adverse possession after 30 years. You can search Companies House for dissolved companies that may have owned specific land.

Companies House: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk

sections.heading: How to proceed
sections.content:
1. Search the BVD published list (when available) for estates in your area of interest.
2. Write to the BVD expressing interest in purchasing specific land.
3. The BVD will assess the land and may commission a valuation.
4. Sale, if agreed, proceeds at market value with standard conveyancing.
